beats.text: Every software project travels through the same seven phases. Think of a relay race, where each phase hands something to the next.
Planning comes first. The goal is a plan for the whole project. Its output is the Software Project Management Plan: the S P M P.
Requirements analysis defines what to build. Its output is the Software Requirements Specification: the S R S.
Design describes how to build it. Its output is the Software Design Document: the S D D.
Development turns the design into program code, and integrates the parts.
Testing checks that code, level by level. Unit tests check single modules. Integration tests check that modules work together.
Regression tests check that a new change broke nothing old. System tests check the whole system against the user requirements.
Then the users. Beta testing is real-world use by the users. Acceptance testing is done by the project owner, to decide if the product is ready for release.
Deployment puts the product into production. Its outputs: the delivered system, a release description, and trained users.
Maintenance keeps going after the release. It fixes defects, adds enhancements, and improves things like performance and reliability.
Remember the three documents. S P M P from planning. S R S from analysis. S D D from design.
